title: The portable core and its contracts
request: Everything DCLab learns to solve must be adoptable by DCLab's main product, not only by this R&D studio; the main product stays in its own repository and is never copied here. Start a pure library with versioned contracts the main product can install and map onto its own planners.
spec: dclab_core/ installable as a wheel; frozen pydantic contracts with a version string (ProblemBrief, DataFindings, SolutionPlan, Decision, Review, SolutionReport); make core-schemas writing their JSON Schemas; an Advisor protocol with a deterministic fallback; boundary tests (no dclab_rnd import, only numpy, pandas, scikit-learn and pydantic, Python 3.10 syntax); a studio adapter project to artefacts and back. Done when the schemas are fresh, the boundary test passes, the round trip loses nothing, and a breaking change fails a test unless its version moves.
plan: Read the main product through gh, read only, to learn its contracts (ProblemSpec, ProblemProfile, MetricPlan, HoldoutPlan, ValidationPlan, ExperimentPlan with governed decision points) and its rules (one training path, train-only statistics, a gateway with a deterministic fallback, compact evidence).
Write failing tests first: boundary, contracts, schemas, advisor, adapter.
Write contracts.py, evidence.py, advisor.py and schemas.py; give Decision its own version, since a host may store it alone.
Add the pyproject, README and make core-schemas; build the wheel and install it in a fresh Python 3.12 environment.
Run the dclab-reviewer; fix all 13 findings before anything depends on v1.

decisions.decision: A pure library at the repository root with its own pyproject, depending only on numpy, pandas, scikit-learn and pydantic, never importing dclab_rnd, never training, calling a provider or touching a database.
decisions.why: The main product installs it pinned and must not inherit the studio, a network path or a second pipeline.

decisions.decision: Every output is a frozen, versioned contract readable only with its version, with a frozen baseline per version.
decisions.why: Once the main product pins v1, any silent shape change becomes expensive; the version must move with the shape.

decisions.decision: Model help only through an injected Advisor; None means the deterministic path, and the evidence it sees is a summary, never rows.
decisions.why: The main product sends every model call through its own gateway with a fallback; the library must work with no model at all.

decisions.decision: Facts carry how they are known: stated with a quote, inferred with a reason, unknown without a value.
decisions.why: A host must be able to tell the person's words from the library's guesses.

decisions.decision: The model protocol is called Advisor, not ModelClient, and the pydantic floor is 2.10.
decisions.why: It advises and may abstain; and below pydantic 2.10 the generated schemas differ from the published ones.

change: New dclab_core/ (pyproject, contracts.py, evidence.py, advisor.py with consult and on_error, schemas.py and schemas/ with baselines), dclab_rnd/core_adapter.py (project to brief and plan and back), make core-schemas, tests/test_core_contracts.py.

findings.defect: A breaking change to a contract failed no test.
findings.scenario: Renaming Deliverable.points (a float) to score (a string) and Risk.check to how_to_check, then regenerating the schemas, left every test passing with every version still v1.
findings.cause: The freshness test compared against files the same command regenerates.
findings.fix: Commit a frozen baseline per schema version under schemas/baseline/ and fail when, under an unchanged version, a field is removed, a type changes, a field becomes required or an enum loses a value.

findings.defect: The adapter's round trip lost fields, including the leakage list.
findings.scenario: Solution.forbidden, identifiers, text_columns, metric, positive_label and notes reached no artefact; a consumer rebuilding a Solution got forbidden=[] and identifiers=[], so leaky columns and ids would become features. The test left positive_label out of its comparison.
findings.cause: The adapter mapped only the fields the brief had a slot for.
findings.fix: Map every Solution field and compare the whole Solution after the round trip.

findings.defect: Rows got past the evidence check meant to keep them from an advisor.
findings.scenario: A mapping of 5,000 keys, df.head(50).to_dict('records'), a nested list of 125,000 values, a frozenset, bytes of a CSV, a range of a million and a 0-d object array all passed.
findings.cause: The check blocked a few types and limited only list, tuple and set lengths.
findings.fix: One shared guard (evidence.check): only plain scalars, numpy scalars, mappings and lists; limits on items, keys, depth, total leaves and string length; tables of records refused; numpy scalars become numbers.

findings.defect: The same hole was in the contracts' own evidence field.
findings.scenario: Finding(evidence={'v': {str(i): i for i in range(5000)}}) validated; and np.int64, what pandas .sum() returns, was refused.
findings.cause: The contract had its own weaker check.
findings.fix: Contracts use the shared guard, converting numpy scalars first.

findings.defect: NaN broke the JSON round trip.
findings.scenario: SolutionReport(numbers={'auc': nan}) dumped to null and then failed to read back; in Finding.evidence and Decision.choice NaN silently became None.
findings.fix: Refuse non-finite numbers in every contract and test the JSON round trip of all six.

findings.defect: The published schemas depended on the pydantic version.
findings.scenario: Under pydantic 2.5 and 2.9 all six schemas differed from the published files (the version literal gained an enum); with pydantic>=2.5 declared, the freshness test fails in such an environment.
findings.cause: The declared floor was below the version that generated the files.
findings.fix: Declare pydantic>=2.10 and pin it in the R&D requirements.

findings.defect: The boundary tests missed database and network access.
findings.scenario: Appending import sqlite3, urllib.request and importlib.import_module('dclab_rnd') inside a function of advisor.py left the boundary tests passing.
findings.cause: The AST test allowed the whole standard library.
findings.fix: Refuse the standard library's database, network, process and dynamic-import modules; a subprocess checks that importing the core loads no third-party module beyond the four.

findings.defect: Build output would have been committed and was scanned by the tests.
findings.scenario: dclab_core/build/ and the egg-info folder sat untracked and not ignored; the boundary test's rglob read the stale build/lib copies.
findings.cause: No ignore rule for the new package's build output.
findings.fix: Delete them and ignore both folders.

findings.defect: Adding an optional field would still break older readers, and an unversioned document read as v1.
findings.scenario: With extra='forbid', a reader pinned to 0.1.0 rejects a v1 document carrying a new optional field; ProblemBrief.model_validate({}) stamped an unversioned document as v1.
findings.cause: The docstring promised that additions keep the version, which extra='forbid' contradicts.
findings.fix: Every shape change moves the version (enforced by the baselines), and Versioned.read requires schema_version.

findings.defect: The brief lacked fields the main product's ProblemSpec needs.
findings.scenario: A brief saying 'judged on F1' had nowhere to put the metric; the target mixed a column and a definition in one untyped fact; constraints and deliverables had no status or source.
findings.cause: The brief was designed before the main product's ProblemSpec was read field by field.
findings.fix: Add primary_metric, split target_column from target_definition, and give constraints and deliverables how they are known, before v1 is frozen.

findings.defect: The JSON Schema accepted what Python rejected.
findings.scenario: A non-Python host validating {'task': {'value': 'foo', 'status': 'stated'}} against problem_brief.json accepted it; Python refused it.
findings.cause: Fact.value was untyped and the stated/inferred/unknown rules lived only in Python validators.
findings.fix: Typed facts (TaskFact and others) and the same cross-field rules expressed in the published schemas, checked with jsonschema.

findings.defect: The adapter called every solution field the person's own words.
findings.scenario: A solution written by the intern's model tool before anyone signed it was exported as stated, source person, with a made-up quote.
findings.cause: The adapter did not read whether the solution was signed.
findings.fix: A field is the person's statement only when the solution is signed; otherwise it is inferred with a reason.

findings.defect: An experiment could point at a hypothesis that does not exist.
findings.scenario: Review(next_experiments=[Experiment(hypothesis=7)]) validated with no hypotheses at all.
findings.cause: No cross-field check in Review; adding it after v1 would tighten a frozen contract.
findings.fix: A Review validator checks each experiment's hypothesis index.

measurements.name: the wheel in a clean environment
measurements.gate: The wheel installs and is usable in a clean Python 3.12 with only its dependencies.
measurements.result: Built, installed and used from an unrelated folder with numpy 2.5, pandas 3.0, scikit-learn 1.9 and pydantic 2.14.

outcome: Done: dclab_core with six frozen, versioned contracts and their JSON Schemas, a shared evidence guard, an injected Advisor, a boundary that refuses the studio, databases and the network, and a lossless studio adapter; all 13 review findings fixed with tests before v1 was used.
lessons: A freshness test is not a compatibility test: freeze a baseline per version.
An adapter that drops the leakage list turns a governance artefact into a leak.
Allow-list the shapes evidence may take; a deny-list of types always misses one.
Read the consumer's real contract before freezing your own.
